name: The Emergence of Firms: base pay plus a bonus (Table 12)
description: Axtell's Table 12: µ with base pay plus an equal bonus from output above it. Measured (release, seeds 1–10, 5 000 periods, burn-in 500, recorded 2026-09-30), µ by the paper's OLS: none 2.51; 20, 50, 80 % of each agent's singleton income: 2.31, 2.03, 1.73; the median agent's singleton income 2.45; the mean agent's 2.43. Under the literal reading (eq. 21), base pay is paid even when a firm's output falls short, so at 80 % firms pay out about 2.85× what they make (Task 1); scaling base pay down to output below the kink instead gives a close µ, 1.75 against 1.73, but not the same agents: the firms-base-pay-80 preset's 5 seeds show effort rising from about 0.10 to about 0.24 and output from about 290 to about 674 once pay is scaled, so µ alone hides most of the change. It falls with the base, as the table's does (1.28, 1.26, 1.06, 0.85, 0.99, 1.01), while effort and output collapse at 80 % under the literal reading.
